title: Bridge starts before LUKS data disk mounts - serves zeros for entire volume
description: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-07-11: bridge process started Jun 8 11:44:03, but /srv/dev-disk-by-uuid-611c* (data1_crypt) mounted at 11:47:50. All symlinks in /export/bridge-source were dangling during startup scan, so _scan_mft tracked only 18 of 8164 in-use files ('calculated need: 64MB for 0 files', 'Populated: 0 dirs, 0 files'). All other files serve zeros from the sparse image (verified: image bytes at data-run LCNs of media files are all zero; VM read of a sample mkv via F: returns size=0). Backblaze has NOT re-uploaded since (0 remaining, last uploads May 16) but any re-read/self-heal/mtime change would replace good cloud copies with zeros. FIX: (1) startup guard - refuse to serve if source symlink targets unresolvable or calculated source size is <1% of image size; (2) systemd unit with RequiresMountsFor= the data mount; (3) restart bridge now that mount is up, verify tracked-file count matches MFT in-use file count.

title: Read path converts every ext4 error/miss to silent zeros - should return EIO
description: cluster_mapper.py:538-539 and 558-559: 'except OSError: pass # Keep zeros on error' - deleted/renamed/unreadable source files, and any unmapped cluster (rescan_mft clear window at 2226-2233, reparse unmap/remap window at 4554-4568, lazy dealloc) all return zero-filled clusters with NBD success. nbd_server.py:327-329 pads short mapper reads with zeros instead of replying EIO. This converts every tracking bug into silent backup corruption - Backblaze uploads correct-length all-zero files with no error anywhere. FIX: return NBD EIO for OSError on mapped reads and for unmapped data-cluster reads within known file extents; log loudly. Related findings from 2026-07-11 review: basename-anywhere fallback in _find_source_file (2772-2782) can map wrong file's content; _reparse_mft_record has no sequence-number guard for FILE records (dirs have one at 4084-4091) so record recycling can shutil.move the wrong ext4 file; no ATTRIBUTE_LIST (0x20) handling so heavily-fragmented files map only first extent.
notes:
--- 2026-09-19: fixed and closed ---

This issue turned out to be the root cause of the 2026-09-18 data loss, not just
a robustness problem. Seconds after mount, with no guest attached at all,
ntfs-3g read an index block back as zeros:

    ntfs_mst_post_read_fixup_warn: magic: 0x00000000 size: 4096 usa_ofs: 0
    Corrupt index block signature: vcn 24 inode 5810
    Index lookup failed, inode 5810: Input/output error
    Failed to read vcn 0x38 from inode 65: Input/output error   (x ~11000)

Mounted -o recover, ntfs-3g "repaired" what it saw, and the repairs flowed back
through MFT reconciliation into ext4 as os.remove and open(source_path,'wb') -
one file unlinked and four others rewritten to their exact original size
in all-zero bytes.

FIXED so far:
- cluster_map / run_map read paths raise IOError instead of keeping zeros on
  OSError (f37688b).
- The image fallthrough no longer fabricates: a cluster that $Bitmap marks
  allocated, that nothing mapped, and that is empty in the image now raises
  IOError -> EIO (6c9fd65). Free clusters still read as zeros, metadata
  clusters are untouched, and nothing escalates before the bitmap cache loads.
- nbd_server no longer pads a short mapper read with zeros; it replies EIO
  (6c9fd65).

RESOLVED 2026-09-19. The guard first keyed on content - "allocated and empty" -
which only caught clusters the image had never been populated with. A cluster
left unmapped mid-rescan (2226-2233) or mid-reparse (4554-4568) still holds its
previous, plausible-looking bytes, and no content test can tell those from real
data.

Provenance made an ownership test possible instead. Every client write records
its cluster in a bitmap (_mark_guest_written, set from _write_inner), so the
read path can now ask who owns a cluster rather than what it looks like:

  metadata        the image is authoritative - _collect_metadata_clusters()
                  covers the system files, every directory (so $INDEX_ALLOCATION
                  blocks), extension records and named streams
  guest-written   a client write to an unmapped cluster lands in the image, so
                  those bytes are the client's own and are returned
  free in $Bitmap a hole; zeros are the truth
  anything else   file data ext4 owns that we have lost track of -> EIO

Both named windows are covered, because neither leaves a cluster mapped OR
guest-written. Nothing escalates before the bitmap cache loads, so startup is
unaffected.

tests/test_unaccounted_clusters.py covers all five cases, including the stale
non-zero cluster that the content test served happily.
close_reason: Fixed across 6c9fd65 (stop fabricating zeros; nbd_server replies EIO rather than padding short reads) and the follow-up ownership test, which replaces the content check so a cluster holding stale non-zero bytes mid-rescan/mid-reparse also fails loudly.

title: Bridge worker truncates last cluster (~64KB) when writing files to ext4 — TAIL damage on every Windows-side write
notes:
Root cause:

bridge.py:_check_new_file (cluster_mapper.py:4316-4344) fires when Windows updates the MFT data_runs for a file. Windows updates data_runs EARLY in a write sequence — before all clusters have data. The worker reads cluster bytes from self.image at that moment (incomplete) and writes them to ext4. Then sets up cluster_map pointing to ext4.

After cluster_map is set up, NTFS reads of that file go through cluster_map -> ext4. The ext4 file contains zeros for clusters Windows hadn't yet written. Windows continues writing those clusters, but those writes now go through cluster_map -> ext4 at correct offsets (so writes after cluster_map setup land correctly). But the worker only fires once per record per MFT update; subsequent writes by Windows that PRE-DATED the cluster_map setup but POST-DATED the worker's read-from-image step are lost — they're in image but reads go to ext4 which has zeros there.

Fix: NTFS provides init_size at offset +56 of non-resident DATA attribute. While Windows is still writing, init_size < data_size (+48). When write completes, init_size == data_size.

_check_new_file now extracts init_size and defers materialization (returns None) while init_size < data_size. The record stays untracked, so the worker re-checks it on each subsequent MFT update. When init_size catches up, materialization proceeds with all cluster data present in self.image.

Added _extract_init_size helper alongside _extract_file_size.

Caveat: pure sparse files (init_size < data_size in steady state) will never materialize via this path. Sparse files are rare for typical Windows app writes; if encountered, will need a separate handling (likely a quiet-period timeout).

--- 2026-09-19: CLOSED, fix verified in tree ---

The init_size deferral described above is implemented: _check_new_file extracts
init_size (+56 of the non-resident DATA attribute) via _extract_init_size and
returns None while init_size < data_size, so the record stays untracked and the
worker re-checks it on the next MFT update. Landed in 5afaf17.

Confirmed against the live damage: every tail-damaged file recovered on
2026-09-18 had a size that was an exact multiple of the 64KiB cluster
(sizes withheld), against true sizes of their true sizes - the signature of a file inflated to a full cluster with the
added tail left zero. That inflation is what this issue describes.

Caveat recorded at the time still stands: a genuinely sparse file
(init_size < data_size in steady state) never materialises via this path and
would need a quiet-period timeout.

title: Bridge fails to protect INDEX_ALLOC in extent records, causing root-dir corruption on restart
notes:
Root cause analysis:

Encountered 2026-05-14 after a large remux swap + bridge restart. Symptom: F:\ root unreadable in Windows VM, OperationalStatus Unknown, Size 0. ntfsfix log: 'Corrupt resident attribute 0xa0 in MFT record 5'.

MFT record 5 inspection: has ATTRIBUTE_LIST (0x20 non-res) — root-dir attributes overflowed beyond one record. Real 0xA0 is in an extent record. Bridge's protection mechanism never sees it.

Three gaps:

1. bridge.py:_fix_index_alloc_data_sizes() (line 903): filter 'if not (flags & 0x2): continue' skips non-directory records including extent records linked via ATTRIBUTE_LIST.

2. bridge.py:_fix_index_alloc_data_sizes() (line 915): 'if at == 0xA0 and rec[p + 8]' skips already-corrupted (resident-flagged) INDEX_ALLOC instead of repairing it.

3. cluster_mapper.py:_mft_write_to_image (lines 740-752): re-patch logic preserves data_size/init_size/INDEX_BITMAP value but does NOT preserve the non-resident flag at offset +8. A Windows write that clears this flag is not reverted.

Fix:
- Remove the directory-flag filter
- When 0xA0 found with non_res=0, set byte +8 back to 1 and write via redo_fixups (just the flag; trust other fields are still intact since usually only the flag flips)
- Also register protection regardless of resident state once repaired
- In live-write re-patch: write 1 to byte +8 of the protected attribute

--- 2026-09-19: CLOSED, all four gaps now fixed ---

The three gaps in the original analysis landed in 4866285: the directory-flag
filter is gone (extent records linked via ATTRIBUTE_LIST are scanned), a 0xA0
found with non_res=0 is repaired in place rather than skipped, and the live
re-patch in _mft_write_to_image writes 1 to byte +8.

A fourth gap surfaced on 2026-09-18 and is fixed in a502fa7. _protected_ia_sizes
stores the offsets found at the startup scan, and the re-patch trusted them
blindly. Windows converts $INDEX_BITMAP from resident to non-resident once a
directory outgrows its record, and the two layouts are different shapes: a
resident value lives at +value_offset, a non-resident header has allocated_size
at +40. A 12-byte all-ones bitmap at value offset 0x20 then lands on +40..+43
and leaves allocated_size = 4294967295. Observed live on the affected volume as
"Corrupt non resident attribute 0xb0 in MFT record 10201".

The re-patch now re-validates both attribute headers against the record as it
exists at write time and skips (logging once) when either has moved or changed
shape. tests/test_ia_protection_stale_offsets.py reproduces the exact
4294967295 on the pre-fix code.
